dedupe_keys.name: global drought hazard spei 6 extreme value return period rasters

description: The Global Drought Hazard project is a set of global raster datasets from statistical extreme value analyses of the 6-month Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index, used to identify areas of high drought risk. The source is the monthly Global SPEI Database of the Climatology and Climate Services Laboratory for January 1902 to December 2018 at about 0.5 degree resolution; the values were converted into time series for each grid cell and modelled to estimate how often SPEI thresholds are exceeded. Rasters are given for SPEI thresholds such as 2.5 and 3.0 and return periods of 25, 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1,000 years. The data were produced by Daniel Weller and Holger Mann in 2022 and published by the IFHV on the Humanitarian Data Exchange as downloadable GeoTIFF files under CC BY. Caveats: the providers state that it is based on analyses of other spatial datasets and should not be used for local or regional applications, and that because of the generalised statistical approach some areas may be under- or overestimated. It is useful for global hazard exposure screening of water, agriculture and energy infrastructure to drought and for climate adaptation prioritisation; a related record is the WorldRiskIndex, from the same institute.
name: Global Drought Hazard (SPEI-6 extreme value return period rasters)
notes: Reference: Weller, D., Mann, H. (2022). Global Drought Hazard. A global raster data set of extreme value analyses of the SPEI.
provider: Institute for International Law of Peace and Armed Conflict (IFHV), Ruhr University Bochum (Weller and Mann)
